title: The Index: stats.json
description: The sweep's own totals, and the site's only clock. Every timestamp rendered anywhere on the site is swept_at_utc, and every number the site states about its own sweep is one of these fields. Numbers here are READINGS: they change every night, they are computed at build time, and they must never appear as a literal in a template or in src/data/facts.json. facts.json holds the other species, external citations, which are static and verbatim. The build checks that these numbers reconcile against jobs.json and kills.json before a single page renders.

fixture.description: True only for a labelled build fixture. Unlabelled data older than 48 hours fails the build, because a site that says verified last night cannot be built from data that is not last night's.

swept_at_utc.description: The one instant, and the sweep's only identifier. Shape is checked, freshness is checked, and every record in jobs.json has to carry it as last_verified. There is deliberately no sweep_number beside it: a counter can be miscounted and a test run inflates it, where an instant cannot be incremented by accident.

pulled.description: Postings pulled. Equal to verified_live plus killed: everything pulled was either verified or killed, and a third outcome is a state nobody designed.

verified_live.description: Equal to the number of records in jobs.json whose status is live or re_verified.

killed.description: Equal to the number of records in kills.json, held records included. A held record is still a kill the sweep made; it is only a record the site does not publish.

killed_by_rule.description: One count per rule the machine can fire, and every rule appears every night whether or not it found anything. A rule missing from this object reads as a rule that was never run, which is the reading the zeroes exist to prevent. The keys are exactly the kill_rule enum in kills.schema.json: 'evergreen' is absent because it was retired, so an export republishing a historic age-based kill is rejected here rather than counted.

killed_unattributed.description: Kills carrying no rule the current taxonomy can name. Sweep 001 has fourteen: every one of them fired the evergreen rule, which was retired on 2026-08-19 for inferring intent from a duration, so there is no honest rule name left to file them under. The sum of killed_by_rule plus this equals killed, and the build checks that. It is not a bin for anything inconvenient: the machine names the rule that fired, and this counts only records that predate a rule existing.
